newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says no plans to devalue baht.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says no plans to devalue baht.

text.p: Thailand's finance minister Amnuay Viravan said on Tuesday there were no plans to devalue the Thai baht.

"We are happy with our currency value," he told a foreign correspondents' dinner meeting in response to a question about whether Thailand had plans to devalue the baht given current external pressure on the currency.
"I don't believe in the assumption that baht devaluation is a quick fix for economic problems," he said.

The Thai baht came under speculative attack last year by investors worried about Thailand's economic problems which include a wide current account deficit, sagging export growth and a stock market that is near four-year lows.
However, Ammnuay did not rule out that changes could in future be made to the way the baht exchange rate is fixed to the U.S. dollar.
Currently the Central Bank fixes the mid-rate value of the currency on a daily basis against the dollar, based on a basket of currencies dominated by the dollar.
The baht was quoted at 25.645/650 to the dollar at 0435 GMT on Tuesday, compared with 25.630/635 late on Monday.
"We are not saying that we will fix the baht forever," he said. "But the change will be because of market forces and not speculation."
"I honestly don't believe that our trade structure will need baht devaluation," he said.
"I believe the economy will become more stable when we can improve performance and narrow the current account deficit."
